grid.note: EVEN columns sit half a hex lower than odd ones (e.g. label 1300 at y~100, 1400 at y~167, 1500 at y~100). Hex-number labels sit 0.36 hex above the hex centre (LABEL_DY=-0.36, measured from printed hex corners; with -0.32 every fitted corner was ~5 px too high). Fit: grid.Mapper (sigma 3 grid units) on 32 legible labels plus 28 printed hex corners; geometry patched in fit.py without changing grid.py.

mapEdgesVisible.north: Yes: hex-shaped top edge from N1 (x~500) to the photo edge; odd-column row-00 hexes (1100, 1300, 1500, 1700) reach the edge and a brown off-map band fills the notches above even-column row-00 hexes (1000 sits under N1, 1200, 1400, 1600).
mapEdgesVisible.west: Yes: the map's west edge at x~25 is open sea, with a strip of grey off-map land (Cape Circeo, labelled) along the top-left and the N1 box.
mapEdgesVisible.south: No: the photo ends inside the Weather Table (the SW photo continues).
mapEdgesVisible.east: Cut: the photo ends at x~1511, through column 17 (about the west three quarters of column 17 visible). "S" (Scauri?) and "Mo" (Mondragone) appear at the edge.

1000.note: City hex drawn with a white hex outline; grid city symbol, anchor and red VP 4. Land is tan hill colour with darker shading in its upper right; its lower part (about a quarter of the hex) is sea. A major road leaves the city northwards through the top hexside into the N1 entry area. The name "Terracina" is printed in the sea west of the hex.

1100.note: North map-edge hex (odd column, row 00 reaches the top edge). Upper half carries dark mountain shading (about half the hex), lower half tan hill; not called mountainShade because the shading is only about 50%. Hex number not legible (under shading). Its upper-left side borders the N1 entry area.

1200.note: Tan hill with some darker shading; the Lago di Fondi lake fills its lower part along three hexsides (1101-1200, 1200-1201, 1200-1301). Major road along its upper part.

1201.note: Marsh pattern almost throughout; lake along its top. A dark grey band about 5 px wide follows its 1201-1302 and 1201-1202 hexsides from the lake down to the coast; it is not lake-blue and does not match the key's river or river+marsh symbols, so it is read as the outline of the lake/marsh artwork, not a river (see uncertain).

uncertain: 1606, 1507, 1305: coastal hexes that are mostly sea; their land terrain (clear vs hill) is read from a thin land strip (low/medium).
1100 (dark shading ~50%) and 1702 (~60% of the visible part; east quarter not visible): mountainShade left false.
1502-1602 mountain hexside: shading covers it, but the tan of 1502 comes within ~4 px near the south end (medium).
1605-1706 mountain hexside comes from the full-mountain-hex rule for 1605; the shading edge itself coincides with the hexside.
1701-1702, 1702-1703, 1704-1705 (pass): east ends of these sides are beyond the photo edge.

1201: dark grey band along the 1201-1302 and 1201-1202 hexsides (lake to coast). Not lake-blue (R-B ~ +12 against the lake's -13) and unlike the key's river symbols; not recorded as a hexside feature. If it is meant as a channel/canal, those two hexsides would need a river flag.
1708: sea in the visible west 80%; east part not visible.
Column 17 hexes (1700-1707): east quarter beyond the photo; terrain called from the visible part.

Sea positions far from the coast (columns 5-9, rows 9-14) are extrapolated from the fit (no printed outlines there); their pixel positions may be off by 10+ px, which only matters for the "covered" calls.
notes: Hex outlines are printed only for hexes that contain land; all-sea positions (the non-playable sea area of rule 9.6) have no outline. They are listed with terrain "sea" so naval range (within 2 hexes of that sea area) can be computed.

Mountain hexsides: rule 2.2.2 (the whole hexside covered by mountain shading; for coastal sides the whole land part) and the key's Mountain Hexside example (dark shading straddling the side). Measured on a 2-px-blurred photo: points 5 px either side of the fitted hexside at 24 positions; a point is dark when its lightness is below 66 (dark tone ~45-55, tan hill ~85-90). Sides with nearly all points dark on both sides were then checked by eye at 3-6x; borderline ones were decided by eye (shadeCoverPct is the measured share).

No rivers, bridges, airfields or landmarks are printed in this photo. The only water feature inland is Lago di Fondi, recorded as lake hexsides 1101-1200, 1200-1201, 1200-1301 and 1201-1301 (the lake also bulges into 1200, 1201 and 1301).
Roads were traced as polylines (roads.json) and assigned to hexes by nearest fitted hex centre; three crossings within ~10-13 px of a corner (1300-1400, 1400-1501, 1506-1606) were confirmed at 7x.
City symbol in the key = grid-patterned block; Terracina and Formia use it and are named in normal case, so both are minor cities. Their hexes also get a white outline.
Fondi and Itri are town circles. Sperlonga and Gaeta have only an anchor (port) and a name, no town circle.
